clue.text: To wash is sort of routine

definitions.meaning: an argument that washes holds up under scrutiny, is credible
a comedian's solo act delivered to an audience, a comedy routine

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an excuse that washes is believable, and a solo comedy act is that kind of routine.

clue.text: Drain made by bore with time running out

indicators.note: time running out means the letter for time leaves the word

parts.note: bore as the past of bear, tolerated, as in stuck it out

explanation.surface: A tedious person exhausts you as the clock ticks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tedious person but is the past tense of bear, endured; 'running out' removes T.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain a glass or straw dry is to draw the liquid out by mouth, a synonym.

clue.text: Sailor departs during New Year's Day for African city

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of another

parts.note: the first of January, written 1 JAN with the one as I
D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables

explanation.surface: A seaman leaves port on the first day of the year, bound for Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of 1 JAN becomes the letter I; 'during' puts D inside it after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Abidjan is the largest city of Ivory Coast, in West Africa, so it is an example.

clue.text: Fancied ringing English club, finally finding correct code?

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: dug is dated slang for liked or fancied

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of club

explanation.surface: Someone keen on an English club finally finds a way to put things right.
explanation.definitionFit: Programmers remove the errors from software code, a computing term, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Quality front row with key series from top row

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
E, R, T, Y run consecutively along the top row of a QWERTY keyboard

explanation.surface: A rugby front row strong enough to be the key part of the team's top line.
explanation.walkthrough: The top keyboard row reads QWERTYUIOP, which supplies a run of keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic or attribute of something, as in the properties of a metal, synonym.

clue.text: Language students doing homework maybe overheard start of Conference address?

indicators.note: overheard signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: Conference is a pear variety; opening a speech to such fruit would be O, pears

explanation.surface: Foreign students hear the opening words of a conference speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a common British pear variety; an address to them begins 'O pears'.
explanation.definitionFit: Young foreigners who live with a family, help in the house and learn the language, e.g. doing homework.

clue.text: Hacks off announcing a report, for example

indicators.note: announcing means the phrase is spoken out, so it is heard

parts.note: a report such as a gunshot is a noise

explanation.surface: Someone irritates people by announcing a report as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacked off is British slang for fed up, so hacks off means irritates, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Letters to keep burning? I'm obliged to return copy

indicators.note: to keep means to hold another piece inside

parts.note: post is mail, the letters delivered
burning means very hot

indicators.note: return means the word for thanks is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, I'm obliged

explanation.surface: Someone asks for letters to be kept burning and offers thanks for returning a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' signals the container and 'return' the reversal; 'burning' looks like fire for the letters but just means hot. TA is British informal for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic duplicate of a document, from a trade name for the copying machine.

clue.text: One not believing that diamonds have dropped down from fence?

indicators.note: in a down entry, dropped down sends a letter towards the bottom

parts.note: an infidel is an unbeliever
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An unbeliever doubts that gems have fallen from a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped down' moves D from the middle of INFIDEL to near the end. 'diamonds' suggests baseball, but is the suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptically, the inner field lies in from the boundary fence of a cricket or baseball ground.

clue.text: Pays in part for smashing decoration to be sent by jet

definitions.text: decoration to be sent by jet

indicators.note: smashing breaks the words apart, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A partial payment for breaking something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti-style paint comes out as a fine jet from an aerosol can, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Member with drink seen by entrance to country retreat

indicators.note: entrance to means the first letter of country

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: A member with a drink spotted at the door of a country retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a noun for a house in the country; it is a verb's noun of backing down.
explanation.definitionFit: A backing down from a position taken, synonym of a retreat in argument.

clue.text: Start with our leading lady present

parts.note: the off is the start of a race
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen at the time

explanation.surface: Begin with a gift for our leading lady.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to proffer or tender it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Gag from the pen of Spooner? Line causing mischief

indicators.note: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: a piggery is a pig pen
a gag is a joke
RY is the abbreviation for railway line

explanation.surface: A joke penned by Dr Spooner causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the pen' looks like writing but means a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceitful underhand dealing, trickery, a synonym of mischief.

clue.text: Pole set off with others for entertainment venue

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole
to trip an alarm is to set it off
joint means shared with others

explanation.surface: A pole is put up alongside others in a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests pole dancing, apt for the venue, but gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: A club staging striptease shows is a place of adult entertainment.

clue.text: Possible forger in mint worked with this

indicators.note: worked means the letters are worked over into new order

explanation.surface: A counterfeiter at the Mint did the job with this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' suggests counterfeiting coins; it means one who forges metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman working tin plate may forge metal objects, so may be a forger.

clue.text: British given to support way of working with large company

indicators.note: in a down entry, to support means to come under the other piece

parts.note: MO, modus operandi, is a way of working
handed means given

explanation.surface: A British gift backs a method of working.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a gang, in force with many people, British informal.

clue.text: Bowls laid at supper around bottles

indicators.note: around means the letters run backwards
bottles means contains, the letters are held in the words

explanation.surface: Bowls are set out on the table at supper, with bottles around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowls' looks like dishes or the game; it means arenas. 'bottles' holds the letters reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is an amphitheatre-shaped sports ground, so stadiums are bowls.

clue.text: In transport project, including most of big network

indicators.note: including means holding the rest inside

parts.note: to project is to jut out

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: big taken as written, then shortened
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: Talk of a transport project involving most of a large network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims BIG to BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in transports of delight is being overjoyed, an idiom.

clue.text: The setter's most reliable reference work's not left down!

parts.note: the setter is, I'm

indicators.note: not means without, leaving out a letter

parts.note: a bible is a definitive reference book

explanation.surface: The setter laments a trusted reference book that has fallen down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like fallen; it is the imperative to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To down a drink is to swallow it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: High-flier, live, intercepted by neat tackle

indicators.note: intercepted by puts the other piece in the middle

parts.note: to be is to live
neat is an old word for cattle, of which an ox is one
kit is equipment, tackle

explanation.surface: A rugby flier, still live, is cut off by a neat tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy; it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A box-shaped kite flies high, a playful description.

clue.text: Poet may write it as exercise

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: A poet might write something by way of practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza of four lines, a common verse form that poets compose.

clue.text: A good thing convent has Roman name

parts.note: a convent of nuns has no men

explanation.surface: A good thing the convent has a Roman name.
explanation.walkthrough: The nuns' convent is a place with no men.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman's extra name added to the family name, like Africanus for Scipio.

clue.text: Articulated lorry, van or bike is initially, but not taxi

definitions.meaning: articulated means spoken, put into words

definitions.text: lorry, van or bike is initially, but not taxi
definitions.meaning: the consonants opening lorry, van and bike sound with the vocal cords, the one opening taxi does not

explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulated lorry' reads as a truck, but 'Articulated' is a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken aloud, and in phonetics the vocal cords vibrate for L, V and B, but not for T.

clue.text: Up at six to join manoeuvres being put together

indicators.note: manoeuvres means the letters are moved into new positions

explanation.surface: Soldiers rise at six to take part in manoeuvres.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing things side by side, next to each other, the noun sense.

clue.text: American, I love pasty

parts.note: O is love, the zero score in tennis
wan means pale, pasty-faced

explanation.surface: An American says he loves a Cornish pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like the pie but is the adjective, pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a Midwest state of the USA is an example of an American.

clue.text: What makes you (think the grass might be) greener?

definitions.text: What makes you (think the grass might be) greener?

parts.words: What makes you (think the grass might be) greener?
parts.note: people are green with jealousy, and covet a neighbour's greener grass

explanation.definitionFit: Being green with jealousy is the idiom; resentful longing makes others' grass look greener.

clue.text: Work on war papers covering trouble after revolution

indicators.note: covering means placed round the other piece

parts.note: ID, identity papers

indicators.note: after revolution means the word is turned round

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Research on war documents covering the trouble after a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' signals the container and 'after revolution' the reversal; 'Work on war' looks like research but is a literary work.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem is about the Trojan War, a literary work on war.

clue.text: She does what singers do, without scores, mostly

parts.note: singers are people who singe, and to singe is to char

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: scores of things means many

explanation.surface: A woman sings as singers do, without musical scores, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singers' reads as vocalists; it means people who singe. 'mostly' trims MANY to MAN. A daily cleaner 'does' for an employer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaning lady is said to do for the household, British informal.

clue.text: Turned, using saw to set about cedar, finally

indicators.note: set about means placed around the other piece

parts.note: to see to something is to tend it

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of cedar

explanation.surface: A carpenter turned wood, using a saw on cedar at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the tool; with 'to' it is the past of see to.
explanation.definitionFit: To trend is to veer or turn in a direction, so trended means turned.

clue.text: Film recalled girl's occupation

indicators.note: recalled means the word is called back, read in reverse

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an alien
Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A film recalled a girl's job.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupying a house as tenant, the period of residence, a synonym.
